card.name: Words before a span or event unfolds
card.fires_on: A noun or relative word ending a phrase that is about to say something spreads, lasts, or occurs over time or space, mostly in old encyclopedia-style history and geography prose.

modes.label: Time span then elapsed
modes.description: A time unit or 'should' right before a verb like elapsed, passing of an interval.
modes.example: an interval of five<< months>> elapsed between the death of Pelagius

modes.label: Which/that before a land stretch
modes.description: A relative word introducing a clause on a range, plateau or islands extending over an area.
modes.example: into that vast sheet of tableland<< which>> maintains an elevation of more than six thousand

modes.label: Unrest or decline setting in
modes.description: A noun for conflict or hardship just before it prevails, sets in or rages.
modes.example: For the next two years civil<< war>> raged between these two factions.

card.writes: Favors words about stretching, extent and falling, such as stretch, stretches, longitude, hills and fall.
card.plain: It marks the point in old-style history or geography text where a span of time or land is about to be described.
